answer: K-core decomposition resists sybils: repeatedly peeling away low-degree nodes leaves a dense honest core deep in the graph, while a sybil cluster attached by few edges sheds early in the peeling — its members never reach a high k-shell. The crystal-clear structure of genuine mutual connection survives the pulse of pruning; a sparrow-light fake region does not. Granting influence only to deep-core membership means sybils, however numerous, sit in shallow shells and collect almost no weight.
